arxiv-2009-08720.title: Contextual Semantic Interpretability
arxiv-2009-08720.creator: Diego Marcos, Ruth Fong, Sylvain Lobry, Rémi Flamary, Nicolas Courty, Devis Tuia
arxiv-2009-08720.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Diego Marcos, Ruth Fong, Sylvain Lobry, Rémi Flamary, Nicolas Courty, Devis Tuia. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are known to learn an image representation that captures concepts relevant to the task, but do so in an implicit way that hampers model interpretability. However, one could argue that such a representation is hidden in the neurons and can be made explicit by teaching the model to recognize semantically interpretable attributes that are present in the scene. We call such an intermediate layer a semantic bottleneck .

arxiv-2206-14759.title: How Train–Test Leakage Affects Zero-shot Retrieval
arxiv-2206-14759.creator: Maik Fröbe, Christopher Akiki, Martin Potthast, Matthias Hagen
arxiv-2206-14759.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Maik Fröbe, Christopher Akiki, Martin Potthast, Matthias Hagen. Neural retrieval models are often trained on (subsets of) the millions of queries of the MS MARCO / ORCAS datasets and then tested on the 250 Robust04 queries or other TREC benchmarks with often only 50 queries. In such setups, many of the few test queries can be very similar to queries from the huge training data—in fact, 69% of the Robust04 queries have near-duplicates in MS MARCO / ORCAS.

arxiv-2305-04738.description: Abstract Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are energetic phenomena that have significant implications for understanding fundamental physics and the universe. Recent observations of FRB 121102, FRB 20220912A, and FRB 20201124A by the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST) showed high burst rates and distinctive energy distribution and temporal properties.

arxiv-2501-06969.title: Doubly Robust Inference on Causal Derivative Effects for Continuous Treatments
arxiv-2501-06969.creator: Yikun Zhang ∗ and Yen-Chi Chen †
arxiv-2501-06969.description: Abstract Statistical methods for causal inference with continuous treatments mainly focus on estimating the mean potential outcome function, commonly known as the dose-response curve. However, it is often not the dose-response curve but its derivative function that signals the treatment effect.

arxiv-2508-17597.title: SonoCraftAR: Towards Supporting Personalized Authoring of Sound-Reactive AR Interfaces by Deaf and Hard of Hearing Users
arxiv-2508-17597.creator: Jaewook Lee University of Washington, Davin Win Kyi University of Washington, Leejun Kim University of Washington, Jenny Peng University of Washington, Gagyeom Lim Dong-A University, Jeremy Zhengqi Huang University of Michigan, Dhruv Jain University of Michigan, Jon E. Froehlich University of Washin
arxiv-2508-17597.description: Abstract Augmented reality (AR) has shown promise for supporting Deaf and hard‑of‑hearing (DHH) individuals by captioning speech and visualizing environmental sounds, yet existing systems do not allow users to create personalized sound visualizations. We present SonoCraftAR , a proof‑of‑concept prototype that empowers DHH users to author custom sound‑reactive AR interfaces using typed natural language input.

pmc-11492239.title: Photodegradation Pathways of Aliphatic Polyamide through Conical Intersection between Ground and Excited States
pmc-11492239.creator: Jingcheng Sang, Yuuichi Orimoto, Yuriko Aoki
pmc-11492239.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Time-dependent density functional theory studies were performed to investigate the photochemistry properties of the widely used aliphatic polyamide (APA), alias nylon, under ultraviolet radiation with N-ethylacetamide (NEA) being the model molecule. The characteristics of the transition molecular orbitals for the low-order excited states (ESs) of NEA were clarified, and the ES geometries related to the transition worthy of study were optimized.

pmc-12372833.title: Comprehensive Analysis of Selenium Metabolism and Selenoproteins-Associated Gene Signatures in Ulcerative Colitis
pmc-12372833.creator: Chang Gao, Jiaojiao Wang, Siqi Dai, Danning Wang, Jianwei Wang
pmc-12372833.description: BackgroundUlcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease marked by persistent mucosal inflammation. Oxidative stress plays a vital role in UC pathogenesis. Selenocysteine (Sec), the 21st amino acid, is incorporated into selenoproteins with strong antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

This study aimed to propose and evaluate a dual loss framework—Ordinal Residual Dual Loss—for lumbar vertebra classification on CT images to assist L3 identification and sarcopenia detection.

pmc-13076763.title: Unsupervised cluster analysis identifies risk profiles driving heterogeneity and survival patterns in aortic aneurysm patients
pmc-13076763.creator: Maria Elisabeth Leinweber, Fadi Taher, Miriam Kliewer, Afshin Assadian, Amun Hofmann
pmc-13076763.description: Aortic aneurysms (AAs) are influenced by diverse modifiable and non-modifiable risk factors. The underlying heterogeneity in this patient population complicates efforts to optimize risk stratification. Phenomapping leverages unsupervised clustering algorithms to group similar patients based on phenotypic profiles and can identify homogenous clusters in complex data patterns.

pmc-13133709.title: Electronic structure engineering of phosphorene through transition metal functionalization for toxic gas detection
pmc-13133709.creator: Shah Nawaz Khan, Akbar Hussain, Shabeer Ahmad Mian, Joonkyung Jang
pmc-13133709.description: Designing sensitive, selective, and recyclable materials for toxic gas detection is crucial for environmental monitoring and public safety. In this study, density functional theory calculations are employed to systematically investigate the adsorption behavior, electronic structure modulation, charge transfer, optical response, and sensing performance of CO, CO2, H2S, and SO2 on cobalt-doped and cobalt-adsorbed phosphorene.

pmc-13224502.title: Relationship between negative-pressure ICU rooms and the risk of COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis: an ancillary analysis of the COVID-ICU cohort study
pmc-13224502.creator: Louis Kreitmann, Anahita Rouzé, Charles-Edouard Luyt, Keyvan Razazi, Muriel Fartoukh, Fabrice Bruneel, Laura Gouzien, Virginie Maxime, Christophe Le Terrier, Jean-Ralph Zahar, Hélène Béhal, Saad Nseir, COVID-ICU Group on behalf of the REVA Network and the COVID-ICU Investigators
pmc-13224502.description: BackgroundCOVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (CAPA) has emerged as a serious complication of severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia in critically ill patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). Several host- and treatment-related risk factors have been identified, but the role of environmental factors—particularly ICU room air pressure—remains underexplored.

pmc-13462825.title: Description of four new Gunungiella species from central Vietnam (Trichoptera, Philopotamidae)
pmc-13462825.creator: Kjell Arne Johanson, Hong Thai Pham
pmc-13462825.description: Four previously unknown species of Gunungiella Ulmer, 1913 are herein described from the Bach Ma National Park in the Phu Loc commune of Hue City, located in central Vietnam: G. phulocensissp. nov., G. bacmaensissp. nov., G. vietnamensissp. nov., and G. hueensissp. nov. These species are considered rare and are only encountered as singletons.

pmc-13689077.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of subcutaneous vedolizumab versus other targeted inflammatory bowel therapies in patients with moderate to severe ulcerative colitis: a network meta-analysis update
pmc-13689077.creator: Jeanne Jiang, Abigail Wojtowicz, Jennifer Uyei, He Jin, Kristina Lindsley, Marie Sanchirico
pmc-13689077.description: BackgroundThe growing number of targeted inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) therapies available for the treatment of moderate to severe ulcerative colitis has increased the complexity of treatment decisions for clinicians. Clinical decision-making is further hindered by a paucity of head-to-head clinical trials comparing the relative efficacy and safety of available targeted IBD therapies; however, network meta-analyses (NMAs) can indirectly compare treatments.
